A_target.statement:
Let $\triangle ABC$ be a [[Definition:Triangle (Geometry)|triangle]], and let a [[Definition:Transversal (Geometry)|transversal]] meet the lines $BC$, $CA$, $AB$ at $D$, $E$, $F$ respectively.
Then, with [[Definition:Directed Line Segment|directed segments]]:
:$\dfrac {AF} {FB} \cdot \dfrac {BD} {DC} \cdot \dfrac {CE} {EA} = -1$

B_source.statement:
Let $F$ lie on line $AB$ and $X$ a point not on $AB$.
Then:
:$\dfrac {AF} {FB} = \dfrac {\map {\operatorname {Area} } {\triangle A X F} } {\map {\operatorname {Area} } {\triangle F X B} }$
with signed areas.

substitutions.each side-division ratio: a ratio of two triangle areas sharing the transversal line
substitutions.the transversal line: a common apex/base for the area comparisons
substitutions.the product of three ratios: a telescoping product of area ratios

derived.product of the three side ratios: a chain of area ratios that cancels to -1

object_map.reformulation: Encode each segment ratio as a ratio of triangle areas built on the transversal, so the product telescopes.

validity_conditions: Each directed length ratio along a side equals a ratio of signed areas of triangles with a common apex on the transversal (equal-height triangles).
Multiplying the three area-ratio expressions, every area cancels in a telescoping chain.
Signed areas track orientation, producing -1 rather than +1.
proof_plan:
Express each ratio as a ratio of signed areas of triangles with apex on the transversal:
:$\dfrac {AF} {FB} = \dfrac {\sqbrk {A D E} } {\sqbrk {B D E} }, \quad \dfrac {BD} {DC} = \dfrac {\sqbrk {B E F} } {\sqbrk {C E F} } \cdots$
using that all three points $D$, $E$, $F$ lie on one line.

Writing each area in terms of the signed distance of $A$, $B$, $C$ from the transversal, the common factors cancel telescopically:
:$\dfrac {AF} {FB} \cdot \dfrac {BD} {DC} \cdot \dfrac {CE} {EA} = \dfrac {-h_A} {h_B} \cdot \dfrac {-h_B} {h_C} \cdot \dfrac {-h_C} {h_A}$

The product reduces to $-1$, which is [[Menelaus's Theorem]].
{{qed}}
